record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Can the residual or asymptotic integrability of the sine-Gordon problem on the quarter-plane be exploited more deeply, for example through methods such as the Fokas approach, to analyze boundary-induced breaking of integrability?

evidence.quote: It is possible that more can be done to exploit integrability in the quarter-plane {(x, t) : x < 0, t > 0} which is the domain of our initial-value problem. The so-called Fokas method (see [79] for a recent review) is one possible avenue for further progress in this regard.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the sine-Gordon equation
   u_{tt} - u_{xx} + sin(u) = 0
posed on the quarter-plane Q = {(x,t) : x < 0, t > 0}, with initial data (u(x,0), u_t(x,0)) prescribed for x < 0 and a boundary condition imposed at x = 0 for t > 0 (for instance a Robin-type condition u_x(0,t) + 2k u(0,t) = 0 with k a real parameter, which in general breaks bulk integrability).

The Fokas (unified transform) method analyzes initial-boundary value problems for integrable PDEs by formulating a matrix Riemann–Hilbert problem whose jumps are determined by spectral functions associated with the initial data and the boundary data. For "linearizable" boundary conditions, an infinite family of bulk conservation laws survives and the spectral data satisfy explicit symmetry relations; for generic boundary conditions, this is not the case and one must in addition solve a nonlinear (Fredholm-type) integral equation to determine the unknown boundary values.

Develop a framework, based on the Fokas method or an equivalent Riemann–Hilbert approach, that systematically exploits the residual or asymptotic integrability that remains for the sine-Gordon equation on Q when the boundary condition at x = 0 is not of linearizable type. Specifically:

(a) Identify the structure (e.g. approximate conserved quantities, asymptotic symmetries of spectral functions, or large-t reductions) that quantifies in what sense integrability is only weakly broken by such a boundary condition.

(b) Use this structure to derive a tractable description of the long-time asymptotics of solutions on Q, including the spectrum of asymptotic radiation and the production/reflection of solitons and breathers at the boundary.

(c) Make precise the way in which non-integrable boundary conditions (such as the Robin condition above) perturb the linearizable cases, and characterize the obstruction to applying the Fokas method directly.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists: the Fokas/unified transform has been applied to construct solutions and analyze long-time asymptotics of sine-Gordon in the quarter plane (e.g., Riemann–Hilbert formulations and nonlinear Fourier transform approaches), and boundary scattering with Robin (non-integrable) conditions has been studied perturbatively. However, no complete scheme is known for applying the Fokas method to generic non-linearizable boundary conditions such as Robin, and the systematic exploitation of residual integrability to analyze boundary-induced breaking remains an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Construction of solutions and asymptotics for the sine-Gordon equation in the quarter plane
status_evidence.snippet: Riemann–Hilbert problem derived using the Unified Transform (Fokas method) for sine-Gordon in the quarter plane.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist using the Fokas method for the quarter-plane sine-Gordon problem with linearizable data.

status_evidence.title: Breaking integrability at the boundary: the sine-Gordon model with Robin boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the sine-Gordon model with non-integrable Robin boundary conditions and boundary scattering effects.
status_evidence.claim: Boundary-induced breaking of integrability for Robin sine-Gordon is studied but not via a full Fokas-method analysis.

status_evidence.title: Nonlinear Fourier transforms for the sine-Gordon equation in the quarter plane
status_evidence.snippet: Develops nonlinear Fourier transform machinery for sine-Gordon on the quarter plane.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational tools exist, but extension to general non-linearizable boundary conditions remains incomplete.
